profile.notes: Synthetic – for demonstration only. Profile built on the Xero Demo Company (AU) data. IT support, training and project services, Marineville NSW; 3 employees from 20 July 2026. Shortened financial year 1 Jul-30 Sep 2026 under s323D(2A); future years end 30 September (the Xero organisation setting still shows 30 June). Audit required by a s293 direction from a 15% shareholder (Sam Whitfield). First audit; FY2026 unaudited. Owner A in the Xero chart of accounts is Alex Morgan (sole director, 85%), who also keeps the books. Both bank accounts are held with Wattlebrook Bank Limited; bank names such as NAB, Ridgeway Savings and Business Savings Bank in the Xero statement lines and narrations are placeholders of the demo data. Related parties declared by management: Alex Morgan (director loan, overdraft guarantee); Morgan Advisory Pty Ltd. Payment approval limit AUD 5,000. No director remuneration in the period.

risk_register.description: Presumed fraud risk (ASA 240 para 27). Revenue of AUD 32,431 for the three months is 7.7 times the AUD 4,200 recorded for the whole of FY2026; 26 invoices to 14 customers, DIISR 24%; all journals are entered by the sole director.
Six invoices totalling AUD 9,000 (excl. GST) were raised on 16-17 September 2026, including a AUD 6,500 development invoice to DIISR (ORC1026) whose service completion falls close to the period end.

The Business Bank Account was overdrawn throughout the quarter (AUD 10,900.44 at 30 September 2026) and the Savings account held AUD 11,581.23; opening bank balances were keyed on 16 July 2026 as a conversion balance of AUD 19,212.21 credited to 840 Historical Adjustment, and the 30 June 2026 comparative omits them.

pages: AUDIT ENGAGEMENT - FINANCIAL YEAR ENDING 30 SEPTEMBER 2026
1. Objective and scope of the audit
You have requested that we audit the financial report of Demo Company (AU) Pty Ltd, which
comprises the statement of financial position as at 30 September 2026, the statement of
profit or loss and other comprehensive income, the statement of changes in equity and the
statement of cash flows for the period from 1 July 2026 to 30 September 2026, notes to the
financial statements and the directors' declaration. The audit is required by the
shareholder direction of 20 August 2026 under section 293 of the Corporations Act 2001.
The objective of our audit is to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial
report as a whole is free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, and
to issue an auditor's report that includes our opinion. Reasonable assurance is a high
level of assurance, but is not a guarantee that an audit will always detect a material
We will conduct our audit in accordance with Australian Auditing Standards, which require
us to comply with ethical requirements. We will identify and assess the risks of material
misstatement, design and perform procedures responsive to those risks, obtain an
understanding of internal control relevant to the audit, evaluate the accounting policies
and estimates used, and conclude on the use of the going concern basis of accounting. We
will communicate in writing any significant deficiencies in internal control that we
identify. Because of the inherent limitations of an audit, there is an unavoidable risk
that some material misstatements may not be detected.
This is our first audit of the Company, and the financial report for the year ended
30 June 2026 was not audited. We will obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about
whether the opening balances at 1 July 2026 contain misstatements that materially affect
the current period's financial report (ASA 510, paragraph 6): we will determine whether
the closing balances at 30 June 2026 have been correctly brought forward, whether they
reflect appropriate accounting policies, and we will perform specific procedures on them.
Because the prior period financial report was not audited, our auditor's report will
include an Other Matter paragraph stating that the corresponding figures are unaudited
Our audit will be conducted on the basis that the directors acknowledge and understand
(i)   for the preparation of the financial report that gives a true and fair view in
accordance with the Corporations Act 2001 and the applicable financial reporting
(ii)  for such internal control as the directors determine is necessary to enable the
preparation of a financial report that is free from material misstatement, whether
due to fraud or error; and
a. access to all information of which the directors are aware that is relevant to
the preparation of the financial report, such as records, documentation and
b. additional information that we may request from the directors for the purpose
c. unrestricted access to persons within the Company from whom we determine it
As part of our audit process we will request from the directors written confirmation
concerning representations made to us in connection with the audit.
The financial report is to be prepared in accordance with the Corporations Act 2001 and
The current period covers the 3 months from 1 July 2026 to 30 September 2026, while the
comparative figures cover the 12 months ended 30 June 2026. The amounts presented are
therefore not entirely comparable, and the financial report is to disclose this.
6. Form and content of our report
We expect to issue a written auditor's report on the financial report, addressed to the
members of the Company, expressing our opinion and including the Other Matter paragraph
described in section 3. There may be circumstances in which our report differs from its
expected form and content, depending on the findings of the audit.
Our fee for the audit is AUD 4,800, excluding GST. We will issue our invoice when the
auditor's report is signed. We provide no other services to the Company.
Please sign and return a copy of this letter to confirm that it is in accordance with
your understanding of the arrangements for our audit of the financial report.
Jordan Ellis, Partner (Registered Company Auditor No. 300471)
